newsitem.title: USA: ECRI inflation gauge 105.6 Oct vs 105.7 Sept.
newsitem.headline: ECRI inflation gauge 105.6 Oct vs 105.7 Sept.

text.p: The Economic Cycle Research Institute's monthly Future Inflation Gauge edged down to 105.6 in October from 105.7 in September, suggesting inflation will be well behaved in the months ahead.
The index's smoothed annualized growth rate rose to -3.7 percent in October from September's -4.6 percent.

ECRI said the overall index fell for the 18th time in 20 months. "Also, over the past six months, only the two labor market related components have exerted significant upward pressure on the gauge, while the other six components have been flat to down," ECRI said.
The firm noted that the gauge was pulled down by sharply slower growth in industrial materials prices and another decline in the growth rate of real estate loans.
"The continuation of the downward trend in the gauge affirms that inflation will continue to be quiescent in the months ahead," ECRI said.
